newsitem.title: USA: NYC Municipal Assistance seen planning bond sales.
newsitem.headline: NYC Municipal Assistance seen planning bond sales.

text.p: Municipal Assistance Corp of New York City is expected to announce about four bond sales on Thursday, including at least one refunding, a financial source said Wednesday.
"(The MAC board) is authorizing four transactions at once, assigning underwriters," said the source, who declined to be named.

The board of the MAC, which was set up to rescue the city from its mid-1970 fiscal crisis, plans to meet at around 1000 EST on Thursday, when it is anticipated to unveil the planned sales. The announcements are a bit unusual as the board typically does not put forward several transactions at one time, the source explained.

Further details were not immediately available, although the MAC has been considering a plan to use a refinancing to help pay for a $125 million reading program proposed by the Giuliani Administration for elementary schools.

Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, in his financial plan, is counting on the MAC to produce around $250 million from a series of refundings, noted a city source, who also wished to remain anonymous. He explained that the mayor wants $75 million to pay for new school textbooks and another $50 million for a drug initiative, but added that he had yet to be informed whether the MAC had approved the last two requests.
